subject.title: refactor(qqbot): install plugin from Tencent package

question: Should QQBot externalization wait for a pinned Tencent release that owns the complete credential contract, or should OpenClaw intentionally support a mutable package and permanent core compatibility exception?
rationale: The current approach transfers runtime ownership but leaves security-sensitive package selection and channel-specific credential ownership split across repositories.

options.title: Pin and complete plugin contract
options.body: Have Tencent publish the SecretRef and manifest contract, pin the reviewed artifact, retain only one-time migration code in core, and then merge.

options.title: Approve transitional exception
options.body: Explicitly accept npm `latest` and QQBot-specific core credential overlays with named security ownership, monitoring, and rollback procedures.

options.title: Pause the handoff
options.body: Keep QQBot bundled until package provenance and native contract compatibility are available.

recommendation.title: Pin and complete plugin contract
recommendation.body: Have Tencent publish the SecretRef and manifest contract, pin the reviewed artifact, retain only one-time migration code in core, and then merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member owns the current handoff design and can coordinate Tencent and OpenClaw security review.
